incidents.vector: Intrusion method not yet disclosed; Equinor says the attack did not involve a computer virus.
incidents.impact: Internal IT systems, including corporate email, were disrupted; oil and gas production was not affected and no evidence of data theft has been found so far. Restoration timeline is unknown.

incidents.victim: Unnamed Silicon Valley technology and defense company (and its employees)
incidents.vector: A Russian national recruited via Telegram entered the US illegally and conducted physical and electronic surveillance of employees — photographing laptop screens, positioning devices near the company's office for remote access attempts, and using fraudulent identification documents.
incidents.impact: Employees were surveilled and in one case followed for nearly 30 miles; detailed profiles were compiled on at least three employees of the company, which supplies weapons used against Russia in Ukraine. The defendant was indicted on espionage, stalking, and identity-fraud charges.

incidents.vector: Attackers gained unauthorized access to two of Japan's national supercomputers, Fugaku and Rikyu, operated by research institute Riken.
incidents.impact: Stolen data included registered-user details, research data taken from home directories, and SSH keys used to connect the supercomputers to outside services.

incidents.victim: Cryptocurrency holders, gaming-platform users, and VoIP software users (Europe)
incidents.vector: Trojanized installers and lure files, including a fake Viber app and VoIP-softphone decoys, deliver a Go-based RAT and a Python-based infostealer to targeted individuals.
incidents.impact: Deploys the "Overlord" remote access trojan, the "Good Game" infostealer, and a multi-cryptocurrency clipboard hijacker; the RAT uses Solana blockchain transaction memos to store resilient command-and-control addresses.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached a technology vendor that provides SharePoint data-migration services and used that access to steal Infoblox customer data.
incidents.impact: Customer data was stolen from Infoblox's environment; the number of affected customers and whether extortion is involved have not been disclosed.

incidents.vector: Details of the intrusion method were not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Coles disclosed a security breach and said no data has been confirmed stolen so far, though it cautioned that could change as the investigation continues.

incidents.victim: Two unnamed US-based organizations (government officials, defense contractors, NGOs)
incidents.vector: Stolen Google Workspace Super Admin credentials plus an MFA-fatigue attack enabled mass data exfiltration and log tampering; a second case used phishing to compromise a federated SSO account and steal tokens and files.
incidents.impact: Mass email and cloud-storage exfiltration, long-term persistence via rogue MFA enrollment, and downstream targeting using stolen organizational data; new phishing operations tied to the same actor were observed as recently as November 2026.

incidents.victim: Fireworks AI (cascading to Cursor, Uber, Notion)
incidents.vector: A stolen access key issued to AI platform Fireworks was used to breach its infrastructure, then session-record data containing unredacted credentials was used to pivot into Cursor's extension marketplace and an Uber cloud environment.
incidents.impact: Attackers tampered with Cursor's VS Code extension cache to push a malicious Claude Code extension with an SSH backdoor to roughly 5,000 systems, and accessed driver's license data and other PII for 149,346 people via a third-party cloud environment tied to Uber; Notion was also affected. Mandiant has linked the incident to a broader pattern of 2026 "LLMjacking" breaches.

incidents.victim: Indian defense contractors and military personnel (potentially broader defense sector)
incidents.vector: Fake recruiter websites impersonating major defense firms (Airbus, BAE Systems, Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman and others) lured job-seeking defense and military personnel into downloading a trojanized app outside official app stores.
incidents.impact: Deployed GravityRAT spyware to steal contacts, call logs, texts, and WhatsApp messages; the campaign has been active for roughly 12 months and remains ongoing, with tactics that could extend to defense personnel outside India.

incidents.victim: US hospitals, healthcare entities, and schools (6+ states)
incidents.vector: Gained network access and exfiltrated large volumes of data, then extorted victims for payment without deploying encryption.
incidents.impact: More than 50TB of data stolen, including over 70 million confidential health records, with over $500 million in ransom demands; a Kazakh national affiliated with the operation (the "8-Digits Team," tied to the INC and Lynx ransomware groups) was extradited from Italy and appeared in US court on Nov 16.

incidents.vector: Hack of a third-party email service provider used by the city.
incidents.impact: Personal data of 1 million citizens stolen.

incidents.victim: 178+ organizations' websites, including CNN, Zoom, Salesforce, GitLab, Equifax, HSBC, BBC, NPR, and Fox News
incidents.vector: Exploited a vulnerability in the Optimizely Web Experimentation platform to inject malicious JavaScript (Magecart-style) into a customizable project field, served to site visitors from the vendor's own legitimate CDN and certificate; the payload evolved through the day, adding a crypto-address swapper, card skimmer, cookie/screenshot stealer, and iOS exploit kits (Coruna, DarkSword).
incidents.impact: Report URI identified malicious code on 178 affected sites; only about 15% had content security policies that fully blocked the payload, while 68 had none at all. An estimated $7,500 in cryptocurrency was confirmed stolen, with unknown further losses from card skimming and iOS infections. Optimizely patched the vulnerability and removed the injected code within a day.

incidents.victim: French media, entertainment, and education-sector websites
incidents.vector: A system the researchers call "exploit_agent" chains multiple AI agents to compare vendor code before and after a patch ships, infer the underlying flaw, draft a working exploit, and execute it without human involvement.
incidents.impact: Assessed by Google as the first cyberattack run end-to-end by AI with no human in the loop at any stage; victim data found on the attacker's staging server pointed to targeting of French websites, and associated scripts included a tool that erased rival attackers' webshells, though the scale of confirmed compromise was not established.

incidents.victim: Semiconductor manufacturers, US defense-policy organizations, and civil-society groups (19 targeted, 10 breached)
incidents.vector: Attackers directed the autonomous AI pentesting framework Cairn, paired with Chinese LLMs, to independently plan, scan, and exploit known weaknesses — weak or default credentials, authentication bypasses, and exposed APIs.
incidents.impact: Across 25 autonomous operations run in August-September 2026, the campaign achieved unauthorized access at 10 organizations, exposing over 1 million personal records at one victim, obtaining military and government identities, creating persistent admin accounts, and modifying a live industry standards-ballot document.

incidents.vector: Supply-chain attack planted a malicious update inside the company's drone flight-planning software.
incidents.impact: The company shut down its IT network and German defense forces grounded drones supplied to Ukraine's military as a precaution; the malicious file never reached the drones themselves.

incidents.vector: Breach of Maileva's systems; details of the intrusion method were not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Data of 22 million users stolen, mostly corporate paycheck and invoice recipients.

incidents.vector: Misconfigured, publicly exposed database left accessible online.
incidents.impact: More than 125 million SMS messages exposed online.

incidents.vector: Business email compromise impersonating a contractor tricked city staff into redirecting payments to attacker-controlled bank accounts.
incidents.impact: $14.7 million paid out over roughly five months before the fraud was discovered.

incidents.victim: Check Point Security Gateway customers (unspecified number)
incidents.vector: Chained a Check Point Security Gateway remote-code-execution flaw (PHP2Shell, CVE-2026-109618/CVE-2026-109619) with a DynamicCLI privilege-escalation bug (CVE-2026-123039) to deploy a webshell, then a proxy, a wiper, and other components.
incidents.impact: Active exploitation ongoing since late October 2026 against gateways that had not yet applied the available patch.

incidents.vector: Details of the intrusion method were not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Some of the agency's digital platforms were shut down following the incident.

incidents.vector: Data taken from a cloud service provider used by TSMC rather than TSMC's own network.
incidents.impact: Personal data of 46,000 employees leaked after a failed $200,000 bitcoin extortion demand.

incidents.vector: Malicious hardware implants planted in devices sold through an unauthorized reseller between August and September 2026.
incidents.impact: A firmware update bricked affected devices; Trezor cut 80% of its supplier network in response.

incidents.vector: Accessed via a breach at a third-party data platform provider.
incidents.impact: Data leaked publicly after Expedia refused to pay the attackers' ransom demand.

incidents.vector: Exploited a flaw in the exchange's user-accounting system to make unauthorized withdrawals.
incidents.impact: $2.23 million stolen; an additional $3 million in attempted theft was blocked by a rate limiter.

incidents.victim: ActiveCloud (Belarusian cloud provider) and three Russian cloud providers
incidents.vector: Ransomware attack took down services at ActiveCloud; three other Russian cloud providers were separately hit by similar unexplained attacks over the preceding month.
incidents.impact: Web hosting and email were restored, but other services remained down nearly a week after the attack; no ransomware group has claimed credit.

incidents.vector: Upstream breach of Spanish reservation platform Amadeus exposed passenger data.
incidents.impact: Passenger personal data exposed.

incidents.vector: ClickFix-style social-engineering campaign tricks macOS users into pasting a malicious command into Terminal, which downloads additional malware.
incidents.impact: Delivers a cryptocurrency wallet-draining infostealer dubbed "DownTheDRAIN"; Apple has blocked some observed samples.

incidents.vector: Phishing emails impersonating Microsoft 365 service-health alerts exploited a real Nov 12 Exchange Online outage, creating urgency to drive victims to a credential-phishing redirect chain.
incidents.impact: Likely credential-phishing campaign; Microsoft states it has no confirmed evidence of credential capture, malware delivery, or post-compromise activity to date.

incidents.vector: An un-revoked cloud access key issued to a third-party AI provider was used to access its cloud environment, then the attacker deployed the ARTEX AI pentesting framework to escalate access across 10 cloud environments, including infrastructure managing its XDR platform, while searching for cryptocurrency-wallet seed phrases, private keys, and Kubernetes secrets.
incidents.impact: No evidence of access to XDR customer credentials; affected customers were told to reissue credentials as a precaution; the intrusion lasted almost two days and was discovered after an engineer noticed unusual activity on a personal account.
